Illustrative data. Names come from the nuna demo; counts, sizes and times are invented to show a production-sized estate. Nothing here is measured.

Nuna console · redesign for review

A console that shows what nuna does for every table, every night.

Three directions for the home screen, then 14 screens in the recommended one, built in its real palette, type and components, plus 3 phone screens, the design system, and the catalog's branches and tags with every word on their screens (chapter 6). Every panel carries a pin that says where its data comes from. Nothing shown here claims a capability nuna lacks.

How to read the pins

1

Exists today. An existing route serves it; the note names the route.

2

Needs a new route. nuna has the data or the capability, but no route gives it to the console yet; the note names the route it needs.

3

Proposed. Beyond v1: decided in the backlog but not built, such as compaction on request. Drawn dashed and disabled, never as working.

Chapter 1 · Direction board

Three ways to open the console. A sells best because it is the product, not a poster of it.

Each card is the same home screen with the same data, built three ways. They differ on the axes people split on: density, imagery, type and light against dark. Select Open full size on any card to read it at 1,280 pixels.

Recommendation

Build A. Borrow B's answer-first headline and C's waterline for the sign-in screen.

People open a console many times a day, and a selling screen that slows the twentieth visit stops selling. A is calm where the work is frequent and expressive in one place only, the ice line, which is a real index of the estate rather than an illustration. It works in light and dark, it is plain CSS and SVG, and its numbers come from routes nuna has or can add cheaply.

  1. Real product first. A's hero is the estate itself: every table, its state, what the worker will do. Business buyers trust the real interface over illustration.
  2. Delight earned and rare. One 0.9 s entrance that reports success (last night's fixes), never motion on frequent actions.
  3. Honest by construction. Each figure on A's home names its route. C's strata would need byte totals nuna does not keep today.

Chapter 2 · Direction A, desktop

Fourteen screens, colored as built.

Desktop frames are drawn at up to 1,376 pixels, the console in a 1440 screen. With less room a frame lays out by its own width, as the console will, and never shrinks its text; below 761 pixels it takes the phone layout. Signed in as presenter, who is in all four demo groups, unless a screen says otherwise. Press T to see any frame in the other theme.

2.1 · Sign-in

Sign-in: the one poster moment, then out of the way

Everyone sees this page once a session, so it can carry the product's four true claims and C's waterline. The form stays the existing OIDC flow with PKCE; the token box shows only when the server allows it.

https://nuna.example.com/ui/Illustrative data
1 nuna

The Iceberg catalog that keeps every table in shape and every change on record.

  • Four interchangeable stores. PostgreSQL, Oracle, MongoDB or CockroachDB, each passing the same fault-injection suite.
  • Maintenance that respects the rules. Snapshot expiry, orphan-file removal and compaction run under holds, freezes and recovery windows.
  • Every read, change and refusal audited. Changes reach a hash-chained archive kept at least five years.
  • Credentials per table. Short-lived storage credentials, scoped to the table's own prefix, only to callers allowed to read it.

  1. 1Exists today · GET /management/v1/catalogs

    Catalog picker, as now. Name, groups and expiry come from the token's claims, for display only; the server decides everything.

  2. 2Needs GET /management/v1/maintenance/nights?days=30

    The headline counts. The worker reports scans and the last compaction of each table today, not what each job did. Each job report gains counts: files in and out, snapshots expired, bytes deleted.

  3. 3Needs GET /management/v1/maintenance/estate

    One row per table the caller may select: data files, score, reasons, hold, freeze, fixed last night. Height above the line is the data-file count on a log scale, each namespace rising to its largest table, with a dashed reference at 1,000 files; depth below is the score. Signature moment. The neediest list exists but leaves out tables in shape, so it cannot draw the line above the ice.

  4. 4Needs .../maintenance/nights

    Same route as the headline. Until it lands, this group shows only what GET /management/v1/maintenance/scans gives: last scan and failed jobs.

  5. 5Exists today · GET /management/v1/health/catalog

    Platform operators only. Anyone else sees this group's refusal state (screen 2.13 shows the pattern), never a guess.

  6. 6Exists today · GET /management/v1/health/catalog

    The audit's Kafka acknowledgement and failed publishes, from the same answer.

  7. 7Needs GET /management/v1/audit/archive

    Where the hash-chained archive was last checked whole. The archive writer exists (M7); no route reports on it.

  8. 8Needs GET /management/v1/catalogs/{catalog}/governance/summary

    Counts across the catalog. Governance is read per object today, which would mean one call per table.

  9. 9Exists today · GET /management/v1/maintenance/tables

    The neediest tables the caller may read, in the order the worker starts jobs, with each table's reasons. File counts and the last compaction stay on the maintenance page. Score bars are SVG sized by attributes, since the CSP forbids inline styles.

  10. 10Needs .../maintenance/nights

    Each job's start, end and outcome. The catalog keeps only each table's last compaction, so a full night cannot be drawn yet.

Chapter 3 · Direction A, phone, 390 pixels

Three screens people open away from a desk: the morning check, a table someone asked about, and health during an incident.

The same pages, the same code: each frame lays out by its own width. The menu folds behind a button, the tree gives way to breadcrumbs and wide tables become lists. Nothing a phone shows is a different answer from what a desk shows.

Chapter 4 · Design system

One stylesheet of tokens and twelve components, in light and dark.

Every colour is an OKLCH token with a light and a dark value; every pair that carries text is measured against WCAG 2.2 AA. Marks in charts are held to 3:1. This page is styled with the same tokens, so the swatches and the page agree.

Colour tokens

Primitives (--l0 to --l7, --d0 to --d7) carry no meaning; the semantic tokens below map onto them per theme. Five states each have an ink for text, a wash for backgrounds and a mark for charts. Ratios are WCAG contrast, measured from the OKLCH values.

Chapter 5 · What it takes to build

Five read routes, one worker change and one CSP line. Everything else is console code on routes that exist.

The pins on every screen add up below. Nothing drawn solid needs anything beyond this list; anything dashed waits on a decision already in the backlog.

New read routes

Each is a read, audited like every management route, and filtered to what the caller may see.

  • GET /management/v1/maintenance/nights?days=30Per night: tables compacted, files in and out, snapshots expired, bytes deleted, jobs cut off and failed. The worker must also report these counts with each job. Screens 2.2, 2.8.
  • GET /management/v1/maintenance/estateEvery table the caller may select, with its data-file count, score, reasons, hold, freeze and whether last night fixed it; the neediest route leaves out tables in shape. Screens 2.2, 2.3 (tree dots), 3.1.
  • GET /management/v1/catalogs/{catalog}/governance/summaryCounts of classified, held, frozen, regulated and closed tables, and every hold and freeze, for tables the caller may describe. Screens 2.2, 2.9.
  • GET /management/v1/audit/archiveHow far the hash-chained archive was last verified whole, and its Object Lock date. Screens 2.2, 2.11.
  • GET /management/v1/health/storeThe backend, its recovery window and a self-check, for platform operators. Screen 2.12.

The CSP line and the fonts

Today's policy, which the console keeps in full:

default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self';
img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'

Proposed: add font-src 'self', and serve /ui/fonts/instrument-sans.woff2 and /ui/fonts/geist-mono.woff2 from the classpath without a token, as the console's other static files are, with a long cache. If declined, the system stacks take over (chapter 4).

STAYS AS IT IS

No inline style or script, no third-party code, no build step. Every chart is SVG drawn by the console's own modules with attributes, so the CSP needs no 'unsafe-inline'. Pages are built from text nodes with h().

Console work on routes that exist

  • GET …/objects/{id}/exportExport metadata and journal from a table's header.
  • GET · PUT …/maintenance-policyResolved policy with sources and guardrail reasons; editing needs modify.
  • PUT …/attributes/{attribute} · POST …/holdsClassification and holds from the console, with manage-tags.
  • POST …/grants/checkWhich tabs to offer, and the reason a regulated table is closed.
  • GET /management/v1/dr/watermarksThe DR panel on the health page.

Proposed, beyond v1

  • Compact a table nowBacklog 114 (D30 amended 2026-11-20). Drawn dashed and disabled in every table header (2.4 to 2.7, 2.11) and on 2.8; the pin sits on 2.4 and 2.8.
  • Catalog-wide branchesBacklog 109 (D33). Not drawn: the snapshots screen shows Iceberg's own refs only.
  • Activity across the catalogA feed over every object needs the queryable audit tables (D23, amended 2026-11-20). Not drawn.

Words that change

Today's strings, quoted from the console's modules, and what replaces them. The rule: name the thing, say what happens, never make the reader decode.

WhereTodayProposedWhy

Questions, each with the default these wireframes assume

  1. Ship two fonts behind font-src 'self'?

    Default: yes. 53 KB, both OFL, served by the console like its other static files. Declined, the system stacks are drawn in chapter 4.

  2. Add the five read routes, and have the worker report job counts?

    Default: yes, nights and estate first, since the home screen's headline and ice line rest on them. Until then the home screen shows what exists: the queue, health and the last scan.

  3. Which home screen: A, Ice line?

    Default: A, with B's answer-first headline and C's waterline on the sign-in screen.

  4. Should the console write: policy, classification, holds?

    Default: yes for each route that exists, behind its own privilege, with the server's refusal shown as on screen 2.10.

  5. Is a production-sized estate the right sample?

    Default: yes. Names come from the demo; counts are invented and marked "Illustrative data" on every frame.

5.4 · The ask

Approve three things and the console opens every morning on what nuna did overnight.

  1. 1
    Direction A, the ice line

    With B's answer-first headline and C's waterline on the sign-in screen.

  2. 2
    Two read routes, and job counts from the worker

    …/maintenance/nights and …/maintenance/estate. They light the headline, the ice line, last night's lanes and the tree's marks.

  3. 3
    font-src 'self' and two fonts

    53 KB, both OFL, served like the console's other files. The rest of the CSP stays as it is.

of panels can be built today on routes that exist. wait for a read route; stay proposed until the backlog builds them. Every refusal is the catalog's own words.

Chapter 6 · Branches and tags · added in v18 for items 104 to 109

The catalog's branches and tags, every screen and every word, for item 109's builder.

Each screen below is drawn from console_prototype_v14.html, which a builder can open and click through (?user=presenter may do everything; ?user=gary may do none of it; &refs=full shows the branch limit reached). Under each figure: the layout, every state, and every word, with the data each word comes from. Words in {braces} are filled from the data named beside them. Source tags: 106 built on branch refs-106-current (RefRoutes); 107 to build as item 107 says; gap a fact no item promises yet, listed in 6.10.

6.1 · Two kinds of ref, two labels, never mixed

@dev @matter-2026-114

A catalog ref: every table and view at once, read through {catalog}@{name}. Always shown as a rounded chip with an @ before the name, a branch icon or a tag icon, in the ref hue (teal-green, --cref-*; tags a little greener, --ctag-*). Main is shown as plain main, never @main. Sections that list them are titled Branches and tags.

surveillance-review

A table's own Iceberg ref, inside one table's metadata, made by an engine. Always a square-cornered outlined badge in the accent (branch) or held violet (tag), no @. Its section on the table page is titled Iceberg refs in this table; the snapshots panel History and Iceberg refs; its column Iceberg refs. The table tab is renamed from Snapshots and refs to Snapshots.

Inside a catalog branch

Shown on a table's Snapshots tab read through a ref: "These are the snapshots @{ref} reaches. Inside the table, its own Iceberg branch is still called main: the catalog's ref chooses which metadata file is read, and that file's refs are Iceberg's."

6.9 · At 390 px

The tree is hidden as on every browse page. The selector stays in the title area (the table actions box shows only the selector on a phone). The band stacks: text, then its buttons. The ref line scrolls sideways and opens at today. The merge rows stack: name and reason, then versions, then the two-track map. The key is a two-column list.

6.10 · What the screens need that items 104 to 109 do not yet promise

  1. The limits in an answer.

    The console shows "3 of 50" and warns before a create is refused. Nothing gives it nuna.refs.max-branches, max-tags or max-merge-tables. Proposed: the list route carries limits {max-branches, max-tags, max-merge-tables}, or a settings read.

  2. A branch's changed count in the list.

    The list, the selector and the ref line show it for every branch; today that is one read per branch, each walking the cut. Proposed: changed-count per branch in the list, counting only tables the caller may describe.

  3. Rights, before the click.

    Actions show only to callers with create on the catalog, and Merge only with write on each moved table. Proposed: the list and read answers carry may {create} and the dry run carries each table's check result.

  4. The dry run's full answer (107).

    Fix the success shape (moves with namespace, name, kind, cut-version, main-version, branch-version) and the 409's exception name and message; give per table the D11, D24 and D37 checks and the caller's write; for a changed-on-both conflict, main's commits since the cut (count and actors); for a dropped table, when and by whom.

  5. The merge's own answer.

    Return main's new version per table and the request id, so the result can say "Main was 271, is 272".

  6. A branch's own commits.

    The Changes tab lists each commit on the branch (time, operation, rows). The read route gives only versions. Proposed: the read route carries each changed table's last commit on the branch, or the console reads them from the table's journal through the ref.

  7. Refs that ended, and the expired branch that holds its name.

    The list leaves out a branch past expiry; the console needs to say why a name is taken and what ended lately. Proposed: an audit query for ref records by catalog and by subject (also used by the Record tab), or a state of expired in the list.

  8. A purpose line.

    Each ref's row shows why it exists. RefRoutes stores no description. Proposed: an optional description on create.

  9. The cut's time for a ref made from a ref, and a table's cut-version for unchanged tables.

    Shown in the band and the namespace column.

  10. The audit feed filtered by ref.

    The feed's @name search needs records filtered by their branch field.

Questions only Paul can answer, each with the default v14 assumes

  1. Does a commit move a branch's expiry?

    D33, the coordinator's brief and item 26's design say 30 days after its last commit; RefRoutes on refs-106-current sets expiry only at create and renew, and item 105 does not say a commit moves it. Default drawn: a commit moves it (so ci-risk-1184 expires 21 Dec 06:41, its last commit, not 06:12, its making). If not, item 105 or the console words change.

  2. Is main's compaction or expiry "main moved"?

    Under item 107 as written, the worker's nightly compaction or snapshot expiry of a busy table makes any branch that changed it conflict. Default drawn: it counts, and the preview says so. The alternative is to treat a maintenance-only commit as unchanged data and replay it.

  3. Can a merge leave one table out?

    Default drawn: no; the console offers "start again from main". A per-table drop on the branch (reset its pointer to the cut) would let a branch merge the rest.

  4. Does a DR freeze refuse commits on a branch, or only the merge?

    Default drawn: the merge judges each table as a commit on main, so a freeze refuses the merge; commits on the branch follow 105.

  5. Should the console list ended refs?

    Default drawn: an "Ended lately" panel for the last day, from the audit.

  6. Rename the table tab "Snapshots and refs" to "Snapshots"?

    Default drawn: yes; its panel becomes "History and Iceberg refs", the overview's "Iceberg refs in this table".
